title: Wireless wall-switch retrofit using an in-fixture wireless receiver (Ask This Old House)

locations.name: Guest bedroom / home office room
locations.basis: Transcript states: 'We use this room as our guest bedroom and our home office.'

summary: This Old House demonstrates converting a single pull-chain light in a guest room into a wall-switch-controlled light using a wireless receiver mounted inside the fixture canopy. The host explains the historical context of lighting controls, identifies wiring colors (neutral white, hot black, switched leg red), mounts a wireless control module in the fixture, wires neutrals and hot to the module, ties the red switched leg to the fixture, installs a new LED fixture with a brushed-nickel bar, and finishes with a wall switch and system test. The approach avoids routing new conductors by using a wireless transmitter/receiver pair to operate the light, and it highlights common site constraints when routing wiring (attic access, wall notching, structure).

sections.title: Problem setup and historical context
concepts: historical evolution of lighting controls (oil -> gas -> electric)
sections.description: Introduces the room and the single pull-chain light, outlines the goal of a wall switch, and provides a brief history of how lighting controls evolved, illustrating why wiring changes can be invasive in existing structures.

sections.title: Wiring routing challenges
sections.description: Discusses the typical plumbing/structure hurdles to running a new conductor from the fixture to a wall switch, and notes that notching the wall may be required if there isn’t a straightforward path.

sections.title: Wireless switch solution introduction
sections.description: Introduces the wireless receiver/module that will emulate a switch inside the fixture, explains that it will be powered by the existing neutral and hot, and describes how the wireless switch communicates with the module.

sections.title: Fixture disassembly and wiring connections
sections.description: Outlines the wiring steps: remove the existing fixture, connect the grounds, join neutrals, connect the module’s hot to line power, and connect the red switched leg to the fixture for controlled operation; includes mounting the new fixture bar.

sections.title: Wall switch installation and power test
sections.description: Completes the installation by wiring the wall switch, restoring power, and testing the system to verify wall-control functionality.

sections.title: Conclusion and results
sections.description: Ends with a successful test of the wall-controlled lighting and a note on the updated fixture appearance.

featured_techniques.technique: Mounting a wireless receiver/module inside the light fixture canopy to control a circuit without running new conductors
Wiring neutrals and line to the wireless module (white from panel to module neutral, black hot to module), preparing the switched leg (red) to feed the fixture
Connecting the module’s switched leg to the fixture (black from module to power and red from module to fixture) to complete the controlled circuit
Using the wireless switch/antenna to send a control signal to the receiver, enabling wall-switch operation
Installing a new fixture bar and LED bulb to update aesthetics and longevity
Wall switch mounting and subsequent power test to verify full functionality
